Spatially resolving observations of molecular gas provide the physical properties of the interstellar medium (ISM) in the local environment of stellar explosions, such as molecular gas content, star-formation efficiency, and velocity field
This enables us to compare the environments between a SLSN-I and a Type II SN located in the same galaxy.

The host galaxy, NGC 3191, is a massive spiral galaxy ($M_* = 5 \times 10^{10}$ $M_{\odot}$) with active star formation (SFR $\sim 5$–15 $M_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$) (cite: stol13; nich17; chen17a; bose18).
Because the SFR of the host galaxy ranges from 5 to 15 $M_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$ in the literature (cite: stol13; nich17; chen17a), we adopt the range as a vertical line in the plot.
(cite: nich17) and (cite: chen17a) showed a (super-)solar metallicity of $12+\log{\rm (O/H)} = 8.8$ and $9.11$, respectively, using the $R_{23}$ diagnostic with the (cite: kobu04) calibration.
(cite: bose18) also found a super-solar metallicity of $12+\log{\rm (O/H)} = 9.0$ using [Nii]/H$\alpha$ diagnostic with the (cite: naga06) calibration.
On the other hand, (cite: izzo18) found a sub-solar metallicity of $12+\log{\rm (O/H)} = 8.49$ and 8.45 using the N2 and O3N2 diagnostics, respectively, based on the calibrations of (cite: mari13).
The map is created from the molecular gas surface density map based on our CO(1–0) observations and the SFR map based on the MaNGA H$\alpha$ observations by (cite: chen17a).
We compare the column densities with the results of spatially resolving CO(1–0) observations of host galaxies of Type Ia, Ibc/IIb, and II SNe in (cite: galb17).
The molecular gas mass fraction ($\mu_{\rm gas} = M_{\rm gas}/M_*$) is 0.095, which is comparable to those of local star-forming galaxies with a similar stellar mass (cite: sain11; sain17; both14).
The gas depletion timescale ($\tau_{\rm gas} = M_{\rm gas}$/SFR) is 0.32–0.95 Gyr, which is comparable to those of local star-forming galaxies with a similar stellar mass (cite: both14; sain17).
The molecular gas surface density is an order of magnitude lower than at the PTF10tpz site ($\Sigma_{\rm gas} \sim 700$ $M_{\odot}$ pc$^{-2}$ over $\sim$350 pc scale; (cite: arab19))
The gas depletion timescale is also comparable to the host galaxies of PTF10tpz (SLSN-II; (cite: arab19)) and SN 2009bb (broad-line Ic SN; (cite: mich18)).
The CO emission is clearly detected with a smooth rotation signature, which is consistent with the H$\alpha$ IFU observations (cite: chen17a).
